consequences: Readers and writers both count from the octet after the size field, and a compound value whose declared size disagrees with what was read is rejected.
Vectors book-composite-decode/encode carry the published octets; book-composite-wrong-size-rejected raises the size octet by one, so the size check is tested rather than assumed.
evidence: The array example is arithmetically exact: array8 size 0x25 = 37 = count (1) + element constructor (1) + elements (15 + 20).
The composite example is exact too, once the authors array is sized correctly: list8 size 0x40 = 64 = count (1) + title (2 + 21 = 23) + authors array (39 octets on the wire) + null isbn (1).
The layout figure (picture.8) places the size before the count and labels what follows as the items.
question: For compound and array encodings, does the size field count the octets that follow it — the count field, the array element constructor, then the items?

readings.name: Follows the size field
readings.statement: size = count field (+ element constructor for arrays) + items, excluding the size field itself.

readings.name: Items only
readings.statement: size = items only, excluding the count field and the size field.

withdrawn: An earlier version of this entry claimed the published example was internally inconsistent, reading its size byte 0x40 against a content count of 63. That claim was wrong: it under-counted the authors array by one octet (39 on the wire, not 38, since the element constructor octet is part of the array). The vector corpus caught the error — the encoder agreed with the published example octet for octet while the vector disagreed, so the vector was corrected rather than the artifact. The clause is now settled by arithmetic rather than by preference.
